strings.name: James Hansen
strings.summary: Hansen studied physics and astronomy at Iowa, first researching Venus before turning to Earth’s climate. He directed NASA’s Goddard Institute for Space Studies from 1981 to 2013. His team developed climate models, and his 1988 congressional testimony broadened public attention to warming. He continued research and emissions advocacy after retirement. His estimates of warming acceleration and climate sensitivity prompted scientific debate; policy proposals and research findings require separate evaluation.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Studied Earth’s climate and communicated climate change publicly, bringing scientific evidence into energy and environmental policy discussions.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Denison, Iowa, United States; born in 1941.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Models and testimony
strings.highlights.h1.text: His team’s modeling and 1988 congressional testimony drew public and policy attention to human-caused warming.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Iowa: BA in physics and mathematics (1963), MS in astronomy (1965), physics PhD (1967).
strings.highlights.h2.title: Research and advocacy
strings.highlights.h2.text: Continued research and emissions advocacy after NASA; some sensitivity and aerosol interpretations remain debated.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Warming acceleration debate
strings.timeline.t1.text: His team published an analysis attributing some recent warming to aerosol changes; other researchers questioned parts of the interpretation.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Left NASA
strings.timeline.t2.text: Ended his institute directorship and focused on Columbia climate research and public advocacy.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Climate book
strings.timeline.t3.text: Published Storms of My Grandchildren, discussing climate science and policy concerns.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Elected to the National Academy
strings.timeline.t4.text: Elected to the US National Academy of Sciences, recognizing his research.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Congressional climate testimony
strings.timeline.t5.text: Presented warming evidence and the greenhouse effect to Congress, attracting broad public attention.
strings.timeline.t6.title: GISS director
strings.timeline.t6.text: Began leading NASA’s Goddard Institute for Space Studies, serving until 2013.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Physics doctorate
strings.timeline.t7.text: Completed doctoral training at Iowa, then began research at GISS.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Undergraduate studies completed
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earned a physics and mathematics degree, continuing astronomy and physics studies at Iowa.
